vopros: Should I pay for a tool that tracks whether ChatGPT and other AI assistants mention my business, or hire someone to get my business recommended by AI?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Yes—but I’d distinguish between “measurement” and “optimization.” As of September 2026, I’d usually spend a small amount on measurement before paying an agency or consultant to “get you recommended by AI.”

AI visibility is becoming commercially meaningful. OpenAI says people increasingly use ChatGPT to discover and compare products, and ChatGPT now has dedicated shopping/product-discovery infrastructure. Google likewise provides reporting for visibility in its generative AI experiences. ([openai.com](https://openai.com/index/powering-product-discovery-in-chatgpt/?utm_source=openai))

The catch is that AI recommendations aren't a new version of Google rankings where an agency can reliably move you from position 8 to position 2. Answers vary with the question, context, model, data sources, and user. OpenAI explicitly says organic product results are based on relevance rather than payment, for example. ([openai.com](https://openai.com/index/buy-it-in-chatgpt/?utm_source=openai)) So I would be skeptical of anyone promising things like “we'll rank you #1 in ChatGPT” or “we have a special technique to make LLMs recommend you.”

What I would do depends on the size of the business:

- Small/local business: Don't spend thousands per month on “GEO/AEO” yet. Periodically test 20–50 questions a real prospective customer would ask (“best X in Los Angeles for Y,” “X vs alternatives,” etc.). A relatively inexpensive monitoring tool can automate this if doing it manually becomes annoying.
- Established business with meaningful organic/search revenue: A monitoring product becomes more useful. Track not merely whether you're mentioned, but which questions mention you, which competitors appear instead, what sources the AI cites, and whether AI referrals/conversions are increasing.
- Ecommerce: Take this more seriously. ChatGPT's product-discovery systems now accept structured merchant/product information through mechanisms such as ACP, and Shopify catalogs have direct integration. ([openai.com](https://openai.com/index/powering-product-discovery-in-chatgpt/?utm_source=openai))
- Large brand in a competitive category: Paying a capable SEO/content/digital-PR person who understands AI discovery can make sense—but I wouldn't hire an “AI recommendation expert” whose expertise starts and ends with prompting ChatGPT hundreds of times.

Importantly, a lot of what is sold as “AI optimization” is still good web/SEO/reputation work: make your business crawlable, describe products/services unambiguously, maintain accurate structured information, earn credible third-party coverage/reviews, and create genuinely useful pages that answer the questions customers ask. OpenAI specifically recommends allowing OAI-SearchBot if you want pages discoverable in ChatGPT search, and ChatGPT referrals can already be identified via `utm_source=chatgpt.com`. Google similarly says its normal SEO fundamentals continue to apply to AI Overviews and AI Mode; it doesn't require some special new “AI SEO” markup. ([help.openai.com](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12627856?utm_source=openai))

There's also a distinction now between earning an organic recommendation and buying exposure. As of today, September 16, 2026, OpenAI is expanding its ChatGPT advertising capabilities. That's advertising, though—not a way to secretly purchase an organic recommendation. ([openai.com](https://openai.com/index/reimagining-advertising-with-ai/?utm_source=openai))

So my spending order would be: fix basic SEO/business data/reputation → measure AI visibility inexpensively → identify the specific queries where competitors consistently beat you → invest in fixing the underlying reasons → only then consider a specialized service.

If you tell me what kind of business you have (local service, SaaS, ecommerce, B2B, etc.) and roughly what you'd be considering spending—say $100/month versus $2,000/month—I can tell you whether one of these services is likely worth the money and what I'd measure.
